newsitem.title: FRANCE: World Bank does not see debt relief pacts by April.
newsitem.headline: World Bank does not see debt relief pacts by April.

text.p: World Bank president James Wolfensohn said on Wednesday it was unlikely that the first cases in a debt relief plan for poor nations would be finalised before next April.

Creditor nations met in Paris last week to work out details of the scheme to ease the unsustainable debt of the world's poorest nations agreed between the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund and the Paris Club last September in Washington.

"They will probably not be concluded, but they will be running," Wolfensohn told Reuters when asked whether the first cases would be ready by the next round of international financial meetings in April.
Wolfensohn had said in Washington in September that he expected the first cases of new debt relief would be dealt with by the end of the year.

He said on Wednesday that the experts who met in Paris last week were making progress toward evaluating which countries would benefit first from the agreement, which is targetted at nations that are already implementing IMF-approved policies.
"There is no instant gratification on this," he said.
A source close to the talks said last week that the first to benefit may include Bolivia, Guyana and Uganda. Wolfensohn declined to comment.
He spoke to Reuters after a news conference called to announce around $845 million in aid to assist projects in the Palestinian territories in Gaza and the West Bank next year.
